project.name: FreeType 2
project.commit_note: The staged ARVO workspace checkout at `_work/src/freetype2` is on commit `a44e20879cefea41663bb36ff4af908cc4146fb8`, not the metadata `vulnerable_commit`. The line anchors below were resolved against that staged vulnerable tree, which still contains the unfixed `ttcpal.c` code shown in `patch.diff`.

classification.classification_note: AddressSanitizer reports `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` and marks the computed address as a wild pointer. Source analysis shows the bug is an unchecked CPAL palette-span calculation on a 32-byte `CPAL` slice borrowed from the in-memory font buffer: a malformed palette start index and entry count move the read cursor beyond that table extent and past the backing allocation.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42540566 (freetype2): Heap-buffer-overflow READ 1 found by fuzz target ftfuzzer [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42540566
bug_description.normalized: The exact 4319-byte `OTTO` witness contains a `CPAL` table directory entry at file offset 4260 with length 32. `FT_New_Memory_Face()` opens the witness as a memory-backed stream, so when `tt_face_load_cpal()` executes `FT_FRAME_EXTRACT( table_size, table )`, `table` becomes a borrowed pointer to that 32-byte slice inside the original font buffer. The loader then parses header fields `num_palette_entries = 0x2020`, `num_palettes = 0x2020`, `num_colors = 0`, and `colors_offset = 0`. Because the vulnerable loader validates only `colors_offset` and `num_colors`, it accepts the table, sets `cpal->colors` to the slice base, and immediately calls `tt_face_palette_set(face, 0)`. There, `FT_PEEK_USHORT(cpal->color_indices)` reads `0x2020` from the first palette-index slot, `p = cpal->colors + 4 * 0x2020` becomes `table + 32896`, and the first `FT_NEXT_BYTE(p)` at `src/sfnt/ttcpal.c:268` reads outside the 32-byte `CPAL` table extent and far beyond the 4319-byte backing font buffer. The fix stores the extracted table size and rejects any palette whose `record_offset + COLOR_SIZE * num_palette_entries` exceeds that extent.

source.description: First project-side materialization of the attacker-controlled `CPAL` table as parser state: `table` becomes a borrowed pointer to the in-memory font's `CPAL` bytes and `table_size` records the 32-byte logical table extent later exceeded.
source.value_from: The exact witness stored in `poc` (SHA-256 `9343b0526559d4db98fb4eeada80b480a5500efb39613d7d877efbeee414640e`) is an `OTTO` sfnt whose table directory advertises `CPAL` at offset 4260 with length 32. `FT_New_Memory_Face()` receives `files[0].data()` and `files[0].size()`, `FT_Stream_OpenMemory()` stores that buffer in `stream->base` with `stream->read = NULL`, and after `face->goto_table( face, TTAG_CPAL, stream, &table_size )` positions the stream at offset 4260, `FT_Stream_EnterFrame()` sets `stream->cursor = stream->base + stream->pos`. Through `FT_Stream_ExtractFrame()`, this `FT_FRAME_EXTRACT` therefore makes `table` alias the existing 32 `CPAL` bytes beginning `00 00 20 20 20 20 00 00 00 00 00 00 20 20 ...` inside the 4319-byte in-memory font buffer; it does not allocate a separate 32-byte copy.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

root_cause.description: Unchecked palette span. `tt_face_palette_set()` trusts the attacker-controlled first palette index, converts it into a byte offset from `cpal->colors`, and never verifies that the resulting palette range of `num_palette_entries` color records fits inside the 32-byte `CPAL` table extent referenced by `cpal->table`.
root_cause.note: The fix adds `table_size` to `Cpal`, computes `record_offset`, and rejects `record_offset + COLOR_SIZE * face->palette_data.num_palette_entries > cpal->table_size` before assigning `p`.

sink.description: ASan sink. The first palette-byte load dereferences `table + 32896`, which is 32864 bytes past the end of the borrowed 32-byte `CPAL` slice and far beyond the 4319-byte backing font buffer.
sink.note: The saved AddressSanitizer stack is `tt_face_palette_set -> tt_face_load_cpal -> sfnt_load_face`, and line 268 is the first byte read in the palette-copy loop.

tainted_value_origin.description: The fuzz target passes the exact 4319-byte witness to FreeType as an in-memory font. All later `CPAL` bytes and sizes originate from this buffer.

parser_admitted.description: The witness is an `OTTO` OpenType/CFF face with a `CPAL` table directory entry, so optional color-table loading enters `tt_face_load_cpal()` during face initialization.

fine_trace.note: The harness passes the exact 4319-byte witness into `FT_New_Memory_Face()` as an in-memory OpenType font.

Source. `goto_table( TTAG_CPAL, ... )` has just resolved the witness's `CPAL` entry to 32 bytes. Because this face was opened from memory, `FT_FRAME_EXTRACT` returns a borrowed pointer to that existing `CPAL` slice inside the 4319-byte font buffer, and `table` becomes the later out-of-bounds base.
Bytes 2-3 of the borrowed 32-byte `CPAL` slice are `0x20 0x20`, so the loader materializes `num_palette_entries = 8224`.
Bytes 4-5 of the same slice are also `0x20 0x20`, so `num_palettes = 8224`.

fine_trace.code:
cpal->num_colors = FT_NEXT_USHORT( p );
colors_offset    = FT_NEXT_ULONG( p );
fine_trace.note: Bytes 6-11 of the same slice are zero, so `num_colors = 0` and `colors_offset = 0`.
The only CPAL extent check passes because `0 < 32` and `0 * 4 <= 32`. The loader still does not reject the later palette counts and indices that will drive the out-of-bounds read.

After the 12-byte header, `p` now points at `table + 12`, so `cpal->color_indices` aliases the first palette-index slot. Because `colors_offset == 0`, `cpal->colors` aliases the start of the borrowed `CPAL` slice.

fine_trace.code:
if ( palette_index >= face->palette_data.num_palettes )
  return FT_THROW( Invalid_Argument );
fine_trace.note: The caller has just requested the default palette with `palette_index == 0`; this guard passes because `0 < num_palettes (8224)`.
With palette 0 selected, `offset` points to the first palette-index field at `table + 12`.

The two bytes at `offset` are `0x20 0x20`, so `FT_PEEK_USHORT( offset )` yields 8224 and `p` becomes `cpal->colors + 4 * 8224 = table + 32896`. No check ensures that this record offset plus the palette's `num_palette_entries` span fits inside the 32-byte `CPAL` table extent.
The copy loop uses `num_palette_entries` as its bound, so `limit` is 8224 `FT_Color` slots ahead of `q` and the function intends to consume 32896 color bytes from `p`.
On the first iteration `q < limit` is true because the palette count is nonzero, so the loop proceeds to dereference `p`.

Sink. The first `FT_NEXT_BYTE( p )` reads from `table + 32896`, which is 32864 bytes past the end of the borrowed 32-byte `CPAL` slice and therefore outside the 4319-byte backing font buffer, and AddressSanitizer reports the 1-byte heap-buffer-overflow at this line.

crash_stack.function: fuzzer::FuzzerDriver(int*, char***, int (*)(unsigned char const*, unsigned long))

poc.trigger: The saved Stage 01 command runs `ftfuzzer` on this exact file and reproduces `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` in `tt_face_palette_set()`.

format.name: OpenType/CFF font with malformed CPAL table
format.contract: Exactly the 4319-byte binary witness stored in `poc` (SHA-256 `9343b0526559d4db98fb4eeada80b480a5500efb39613d7d877efbeee414640e`). It is an `OTTO` sfnt whose `CPAL` table directory entry is `offset = 4260`, `length = 32`; that table begins `00 00 20 20 20 20 00 00 00 00 00 00 20 20 ...`, so `version = 0`, `num_palette_entries = 0x2020`, `num_palettes = 0x2020`, `num_colors = 0`, `colors_offset = 0`, and the first palette index is `0x2020`. In vulnerable `tt_face_palette_set(face, 0)`, those exact fields make `p = table + 32896`, and the first `FT_NEXT_BYTE(p)` produces the saved 1-byte heap-buffer-overflow. This GT does not generalize beyond that exact witness.
